kidsaint: A brilliant scientist and teacher who studied plants, animals and stars and taught St Thomas Aquinas. He used his clever mind for God. Lesson: study hard and use your mind to serve God.
term: A large weight of silver in biblical times, about twenty years' wages. From Jesus' parable the word came to mean a God-given ability.

quick: The year ends with a crown: Christ is King.
His kingdom is not from this world; it comes from truth and love.
Does Christ reign in my home, work and choices?
2026-11-22.action: Consecrate your family to Christ the King this week.
2026-11-22.question: What rules my life instead of Christ?
2026-11-22.special: Feast of Christ the King, last Sunday of the Syro-Malabar liturgical year. The new year begins next Sunday with the season of Annunciation.
illus: In 1927 the Mexican Jesuit Blessed Miguel Pro was shot by a firing squad during the persecution of the Church. He stretched out his arms like a cross and cried, “¡Viva Cristo Rey!” (Long live Christ the King!). Earthly rulers took his life; they could not take his King.

family.explain: Jesus told Pilate he is a King, but his kingdom is not like earthly kingdoms. He rules with love and truth. We want him to be King of our family.
family.intention: We pray that Jesus may reign in our home and in our country.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show that Jesus is the King of our family?”

catechism: Christ reigns; he will come again to judge.
kidsaint: A cheerful Mexican priest who served people secretly in disguise when the Church was persecuted. Before he died he cried, “Long live Christ the King!” Lesson: be brave and joyful for Jesus.
term: King of Salem and priest of God Most High who blessed Abraham with bread and wine (Genesis 14). The Letter to the Hebrews sees in him a figure of Christ, the eternal Priest-King.

quick: A new liturgical year begins with good news: God keeps his promises.
God hears prayers we had stopped praying.
Christ comes through families: make your home a place of preparation.
2026-11-29.action: Take up again one prayer you had given up.
2026-11-29.question: What have I stopped hoping for, and can I give it back to God?
2026-11-29.special: First Sunday of Annunciation: beginning of the new liturgical year (First Set). From today the Anaphora of Mar Theodore is used until Palm Sunday. The 25 Days' Fast begins.
illus: A couple in a Kerala parish prayed for a child for fourteen years. When their daughter was finally born, they named her after Elizabeth. “We had almost stopped praying,” the mother said, “but God had not stopped listening.”

family.explain: An angel told old Zechariah that he and Elizabeth would have a baby named John. God hears our prayers even when we wait a long time. John came to get people ready for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for couples waiting for a child, and for all our families this Christmas season.
family.ask: Ask: “How will our family get ready for Jesus this year?”

catechism: The preparations for Christ's coming; John the Baptist.
The Christian family, a domestic church.
kidsaint: An old priest who served God faithfully in the Temple. When an angel brought him good news, he doubted and became mute; when John was born, he burst into a song of praise. Lesson: trust God, even when his promises seem too good to be true.
term: Syriac for “announcement” (good news). The first season of the Syro-Malabar liturgical year, recalling the announcements of the births of John and Jesus, leading to Christmas (Yalda, “birth”).

quick: We pray for the dead because we believe in the resurrection.
Prayer and the Qurbana help the souls being purified.
Christian hope is a Person: “I am the resurrection and the life.”
2026-11-02.action: Pray tonight for your departed family members by name.
2026-11-02.question: Whom do I need to remember in prayer today?
2026-11-02.special: Commemoration of all the faithful departed. Many parishes have the Qurbana and prayers at the cemetery.

family.explain: When someone we love dies, we feel sad. But Jesus said he is the resurrection and the life. We pray for those who have died, and we hope to see them again in heaven.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family would you like to pray for today?”

catechism: Purgatory and prayer for the dead.

quick: Our body is a tent; our home is with God.
Conversion begins when we remember the Father's house.
The Father runs to meet us in confession.
2026-11-03.action: Plan a good confession this month.
2026-11-03.question: In what way am I still “far off” from the Father?

quick: Authority in the Church is born of love.
Pastors feed a flock that belongs to Christ.
Every Christian shepherds someone by example.
2026-11-04.action: Pray by name for your bishop and parish priest.
2026-11-04.question: Whom has the Lord entrusted to my care?

quick: A Gentile's humble faith astonished Jesus.
Many will come from east and west: the Church is for all nations.
The centurion's words are our prayer before Communion.
2026-11-05.action: Pray for one sick person today.
2026-11-05.question: Do I trust that one word of Jesus is enough?

quick: Repentance that acts is better than empty promises.
Ordinary work done from the heart is service to Christ.
First Friday: ask the Sacred Heart for an obedient heart.
2026-11-06.action: Keep one promise to God that you postponed.
2026-11-06.question: Where is my “yes” to God only in words?

quick: The question is not “Who is my neighbour?” but “Will I be one?”
Genuine love stops and pays the cost.
The Church is the inn where the wounded are cared for.
2026-11-07.action: Give time today to someone others pass by.
2026-11-07.question: Whom do I pass by on the other side?

quick: Christ is the head of the Church; in him all things hold together.
Peter's faith is the Father's gift.
The Church built on the rock will not be overcome.
2026-11-09.action: Pray for the Pope and our Major Archbishop.
2026-11-09.question: Who do I say that Jesus is, in my daily choices?

quick: Our faith rests on apostolic eyewitnesses.
The Father says: listen to my Son.
Glory prepares for the Cross.
2026-11-10.action: Give ten minutes to silent prayer today.
2026-11-10.question: What does Jesus want me to hear today?

quick: Salvation history ends in a wedding: Christ and the Church.
The invitation goes to everyone.
The wedding garment is the grace we must put on.
2026-11-11.action: Come to a weekday Qurbana this week.
2026-11-11.question: What excuses do I give to God's invitation?

quick: The Church is betrothed to Christ alone.
True ministers point to Christ, not themselves.
Joy is letting Christ increase.
2026-11-12.action: Let someone else take the credit today.
2026-11-12.question: Where do I need to decrease so Christ can increase?

quick: Heavenly vision leads to humility.
Jesus alone comes from above and reveals the Father.
Faith in the Son is eternal life begun now.
2026-11-13.action: Make an act of faith at midday.
2026-11-13.question: Do I trust that all things are in Jesus' hands?

quick: Heaven is Eden restored: the river and the tree of life.
We will see God's face.
The Kingdom belongs to the childlike.
2026-11-14.action: Pray with the children in your family tonight.
2026-11-14.question: Do I receive God's Kingdom as a gift, like a child?

quick: Love of God and neighbour are one commandment of love.
Without love, every gift is empty.
Love is patient and kind.
2026-11-16.action: Do one patient, kind act for someone difficult.
2026-11-16.question: Where is my love impatient or unkind?

quick: We are stewards, not owners.
Use wealth wisely for eternity: give.
No one can serve God and wealth.
2026-11-17.question: Who is really my master: God or money?

quick: Baptism really changes us: washed, sanctified, justified.
Holiness is living who we already are.
The Kingdom is entered with resolve.
2026-11-18.action: Find your baptism date and thank God for it.
2026-11-18.question: What decisive step does the Kingdom ask of me now?

quick: The Gospel is bearing fruit in the whole world.
The difference is in the hearing.
Good soil hears, understands and bears fruit.
2026-11-19.action: Name one worry and give it to God.
2026-11-19.question: What chokes the word in my heart?

quick: The Lord disciplines those he loves.
Pruning hurts but bears fruit.
Without Christ we can do nothing.
2026-11-20.question: What is the Father pruning in me?

quick: Thomas brought to India not an idea but the Way himself.
We are no longer strangers: built on the foundation of the apostles.
Thomas's question gave us Jesus' answer: “I am the way.”
2026-11-21.action: Pray for the Syro-Malabar Church and all St Thomas Christians.
2026-11-21.question: Who brought the faith to me, and to whom am I bringing it?
2026-11-21.special: Commemoration of the entrance of St Thomas the Apostle into India (according to tradition, AD 52 at Kodungallur), and the Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
illus: Ask an elder in your parish where your family came from and when it was baptised. Many Kerala Christian families trace their faith back for centuries. Every such family tree has a root: an apostle stepping ashore.

family.explain: St Thomas came to India to tell our ancestors about Jesus. Jesus told Thomas, “I am the Way.” Because Thomas came, we know the Way too.
family.intention: We thank God for St Thomas and pray for our Church.

catechism: The Church is apostolic: built on the apostles.
The liturgical traditions of the East and West, including the Syriac.
kidsaint: He was brave (“Let us go and die with him”), honest (“How can we know the way?”), and full of faith (“My Lord and my God!”). He travelled very far to tell India about Jesus. Lesson: be brave, honest and faithful like our apostle.
term: “The Way”. In old Kerala usage Christianity was called Margam, and Christians “Margakkar”. It echoes Jesus' words, “I am the way” (John 14:6).

quick: The Father's house has room for us.
Jesus is the Way; whoever sees him sees the Father.
The Church is being built into God's dwelling.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today our liturgical year enters its last season, Qudash Edtha, the Dedication of the Church. For four weeks we look at the Church herself: the house where God lives with us and the Bride who waits for the Bridegroom.

In the first reading Moses pitches a tent outside the camp and calls it the tent of meeting. The cloud comes down, and the Lord speaks to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend. God does not want only servants; he wants friends. The Church is our tent of meeting, and every prayer is a conversation between friends.

The Letter to the Hebrews tells us that the tent in the desert was only a shadow. Christ has entered the true sanctuary, not made with hands, with his own blood. When we come to the Holy Qurbana, we are not spectators in a building. With Christ we enter the presence of the Father.

And the Gospel asks the question of this season: are you ready? Ten young women wait for the bridegroom. All have lamps; only five have oil. When the cry comes at midnight, the oil cannot be borrowed. Faith, prayer and love are not things we can collect from others at the last minute. They are stored day by day.

So this week, store oil. Come to the tent of meeting. Speak to the Lord as a friend. Those who wait for the Lord, says Isaiah, shall renew their strength. May our lamps be burning when he comes. Amen.
kids: Children, have you seen the oil lamp lit in your home in the evening? Someone has to fill it with oil every day.
Jesus told a story about ten girls waiting for a wedding. Five kept extra oil and were ready; five forgot and missed the party!
Our oil is prayer and kindness. Let's fill our lamps every day. Say together: “Jesus, my lamp is burning for you!”

opts.a: The Church, Bride waiting for the Bridegroom
intro: Qudash Edtha closes our liturgical year by looking at the Church as the Bride of Christ, ready for His coming.

sub: The Church is the Bride of the Lamb (Revelation 21:2).
Her beauty is holiness, not wealth.
Each of us is part of the Bride.
points.apply: Let the beauty of your parish be holiness, not only decoration.

sub: The ten maidens (Matthew 25:1–13).
Oil that cannot be borrowed: personal faith and love.
Readiness, not panic.
points.apply: Keep your lamp burning by daily prayer.

sub: He entered the sanctuary with His own blood (Hebrews 9:11–14).
The Church's worship joins His.
Our Qurbana is a share in heavenly worship.
points.apply: Come to the Holy Qurbana as to a wedding feast.

concl: The Church is not a building or an organisation only; she is the Bride of Christ.
Qudash Edtha invites us to be a Bride ready for the Bridegroom.
opts.resolve: This season I will keep my lamp burning with daily prayer and weekly Holy Qurbana.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, with Qudash Edtha our liturgical year reaches its final season. For four weeks the Church contemplates herself: not with pride, but with wonder at what Christ has made her. The Fathers of the East loved to speak of the Church as the Bride of Christ, and this season is a time to look at her beauty.

St Paul writes that Christ loved the Church and gave Himself up for her, in order to make her holy, so as to present the Church to Himself in splendour, without a spot or wrinkle (Ephesians 5:25–27). The beauty of the Church is not in her buildings or her wealth, but in her holiness, the holiness of Christ given to her in the sacraments, and visible in the lives of the saints. Each of us is part of that Bride.

Today's Gospel tells of ten young women waiting for the bridegroom with lamps (Matthew 25:1–13). Five were wise and brought extra oil; five were foolish and did not. When the bridegroom came at midnight, the foolish asked to borrow oil, but the wise could not give it. Some things cannot be borrowed: personal faith, a life of prayer, love built up day by day. No one can pray for me in my place. The oil must be my own.

The Letter to the Hebrews shows us the true High Priest. Christ entered once for all into the heavenly sanctuary, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood (Hebrews 9:11–12). In the tent of meeting Moses spoke with God face to face as a friend (Exodus 33:11); in Christ every believer is invited into that friendship. Every Holy Qurbana is a share in the worship of heaven, where the Bridegroom offers Himself to the Father.

So in this season let us renew our love for the Church. Pray for her, defend her, serve her, and do not be ashamed of her, even when her members, ourselves included, are sinful. And let us keep our lamps burning, so that when the Bridegroom comes, we may go in with Him to the wedding feast.

opts.a: Teaching homily: what the Church is
intro: During Qudash Edtha the Church reflects on her own mystery. Let us learn what the Second Vatican Council and the Catechism teach about the Church.

points.h: A mystery, not only an institution
sub: The Church is like a sacrament of union with God and unity of humanity (Lumen Gentium 1).
Visible and spiritual at once (CCC 771).
Born from the pierced side of Christ (CCC 766).
points.apply: Pray for the Church every day.

sub: People of God (CCC 781–786).
Body of Christ (CCC 787–796).
Temple of the Holy Spirit (CCC 797–801).
points.apply: Use your gifts for the Body this year.

sub: The Catholic Church is a communion of Churches (Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2).
The Syro-Malabar Church: an Eastern Church sui iuris with its own heritage.
Unity with the Pope; love for our own tradition.
points.apply: Learn one thing about the heritage of our Church this month.

concl: To love the Church is to love Christ, her Head and Bridegroom.
Our Syro-Malabar heritage is a treasure for the whole Catholic Church.
opts.resolve: This month I will learn more about the heritage of our Church and pray for her daily.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, during the season of Qudash Edtha our Church invites us to reflect on the mystery of the Church herself. What is the Church? Many people think of buildings, or of priests and bishops, or of an organisation. All of these belong to the Church, but she is much more.

The Second Vatican Council begins its teaching on the Church by saying that the Church, in Christ, is like a sacrament: a sign and instrument of communion with God and of the unity of the whole human race (Lumen Gentium 1). She is at once visible and spiritual, a human community and a divine mystery (CCC 771). The Fathers said that as Eve was formed from the side of the sleeping Adam, the Church was born from the pierced side of Christ asleep on the Cross (CCC 766; John 19:34).

The Bible gives many images of the Church. She is the People of God, a priestly people called out of every nation (CCC 781–786). She is the Body of Christ, in which each member has a gift for the good of all (1 Corinthians 12:12–27; CCC 787–796). She is the Temple of the Holy Spirit, who gives her life and unity (CCC 797–801). And she is the Bride, loved by Christ and waiting for Him.

The Catholic Church is a communion of Churches: the Latin Church and the Eastern Catholic Churches, each with its own liturgy, spirituality, theology and discipline, all united with the Bishop of Rome (Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3). Our Syro-Malabar Church, which traces its faith to the preaching of the apostle Thomas, is one of these Churches sui iuris. Its East Syriac liturgy and its heritage are a treasure not only for us but for the whole Church.

So let us love the Church: the universal Church, and our own Church with its heritage. Let us pray for the Pope, our Major Archbishop and our bishops. Let us use our gifts in our parish. And let us remember that to love the Church is to love Christ, who is her Head and her Bridegroom.
Dear brothers and sisters, in Kerala we know a lot about inheritance: land, houses, gold, and sometimes long family disputes over them. Today God speaks to us about a different inheritance.

In Egypt the Israelites were slaves. God said to Moses: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God. I will bring you into the land I promised.” The land was a gift, but the greater gift was God himself: “I will be your God.”

St Peter writes to Christians who had lost homes and property: God has given you new birth “into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you.” No one can steal it, divide it, or take it to court.

In the Gospel Jesus says it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom. The disciples are shocked. Jesus says, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.” And to those who leave everything for him he promises a hundredfold and eternal life.

So let us ask ourselves today: what am I leaving to my children? If we leave them land without faith, we leave them poor. If we leave them faith, we leave them an inheritance that will never fade. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what an inheritance is? It's something precious your parents and grandparents give you.
Jesus said the most precious gift is not money or land, but God himself and heaven, which no one can take away.
Let's thank God for our faith, the best gift from our families. Say together: “Jesus, you are my treasure!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, our liturgical year is almost over, and today the Lord asks us a simple question: what have you done with what I gave you?

In the first reading Jacob works seven years for Rachel, and the Bible says they seemed only a few days because of his love. When we love, work becomes light. A mother caring for a sick child, a father working abroad for his family: love carries them.

St Paul hears that some Christians stopped working because they thought Jesus was coming tomorrow. He tells them plainly: “Anyone unwilling to work should not eat.” Waiting for the Lord does not mean sitting idle; it means doing our duty faithfully until he comes.

Then Jesus tells the parable of the talents. A talent was a fortune. Two servants invest and double their master's money; the third buries his out of fear. God has given each of us talents: life, faith, family, skills, time, the sacraments. Fear and laziness bury them. Faith and love invest them.
At the end the Lord will not ask how much we received, but what we did with it. May each of us hear his words: “Well done, good and trustworthy servant; enter into the joy of your master.” Amen.
kids: Children, if your teacher gave you a beautiful pencil box, would you bury it in the ground? No! You would use it!
Jesus told a story about a man who buried the money his master gave him. The master was sad. Two others used it well, and the master was happy.
God gave you gifts too: a good voice, kind hands, a smart mind. Use them for Jesus! Say together: “Jesus, I will use my gifts for you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the liturgical year ends today with a crown. We proclaim Christ the King. Next Sunday a new year begins with the announcement of his coming; today we kneel before him as Lord of all.

In the first reading a mysterious king appears: Melchizedek, king of Salem, which means peace, and priest of God Most High. He brings bread and wine and blesses Abraham. The Fathers of the Church saw in him a figure of Christ, King of peace and eternal Priest, who offers bread and wine that become his Body and Blood.

Then we hear a sad story. Israel tells Samuel: “Give us a king like other nations.” God says: “They have not rejected you; they have rejected me as their king.” Brothers and sisters, how often do we do the same? We let money be king, or power, or what people say, or our phone. Christ is not removed from his throne by atheists only; he is pushed aside quietly by Christians who let other things rule.

Before Pilate Jesus stands bound. Pilate asks, “Are you a king?” Jesus answers: “My kingdom is not from this world… I came to testify to the truth.” His throne is the Cross; his crown is of thorns; his power is love. And Revelation shows him at the end: King of kings and Lord of lords.
So today, at the end of the year, let us ask honestly: does Christ reign in my home? in my business? in my words? in my screen? Let us give him the crown today. Jesus, reign in me. Amen.
kids: Children, what does a king wear? A crown! And what does he sit on? A throne!
Jesus is a King too, the greatest King of all! But his crown was made of thorns and his throne was the Cross, because he loved us so much.
Let's make Jesus the King of our hearts. Say together: “Jesus, you are my King!”

intro: Today we crown Christ as King. But His crown was made of thorns and His throne was a cross.

points.h: A Kingdom not of this world
sub: Pilate asks: are you a king? (John 18:33–37).
Christ's power is truth and love.
No army, no palace, no taxes.
points.apply: Ask what kind of power you seek in your life.

sub: The inscription: King of the Jews (Luke 23:38).
He reigns by giving His life.
The good thief recognised the King (Luke 23:42–43).
points.apply: Pray: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.

sub: In my thoughts, words, decisions.
In my family and work.
In society: justice, dignity of every person.
points.apply: Give Christ the first place in one area of life this week.

concl: Christ the King reigns from the Cross and invites us to reign with Him by serving.
The question is not whether Christ is King, but whether He is King of my heart.
opts.resolve: This week I will let Christ reign in one area of my life that I have kept for myself.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday of the liturgical year we proclaim Christ as King of the universe. We sing, we crown His image, we carry Him in procession. But let us remember what kind of crown He wore on earth: a crown of thorns.

When Pilate asked Jesus whether He was a king, Jesus answered: my kingdom is not from this world. He came to testify to the truth, and everyone who belongs to the truth listens to His voice (John 18:36–37). Pilate had soldiers, a palace and the power of Rome. Jesus had nothing but truth and love. Yet two thousand years later Pilate is remembered only because his name is in our Creed, and Jesus reigns in the hearts of millions.

Above the Cross the soldiers nailed an inscription: this is the King of the Jews (Luke 23:38). They meant it as a mockery, but it was the truth. Christ reigns from the Cross. His power is not to take life but to give it. And the first one to recognise His kingship was a dying criminal who said: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. Jesus answered: today you will be with me in Paradise (Luke 23:42–43).

So the real question today is not whether Christ is King of the universe. He is, whether the world accepts it or not. The question is whether He is King of my heart. Does He reign over my tongue, my money, my phone, my family, my work, my politics? Or have I kept some area of my life closed to Him, a little kingdom of my own?

As we end this liturgical year, let us open every door to Christ. Let us serve as He served, especially the least of His brothers and sisters. And when we receive Him in this Holy Qurbana, let us say with the good thief: Jesus, remember me in your kingdom. That prayer is enough to save a whole life.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Kingship of Christ in the Church's teaching
intro: Pope Pius XI established this feast in 1925 (Quas Primas), when nations were turning away from God. Its message is even more urgent today.

sub: By nature: He is the Son of God (Colossians 1:15–17).
By conquest: He redeemed us by His blood (1 Peter 1:18–19).
By right: all authority given to Him (Matthew 28:18).
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly, attentive to the words about Christ.

points.h: His Kingdom: already and not yet
sub: Present in mystery in the Church (Lumen Gentium 3).
Growing like a seed.
Fulfilled at His coming in glory (CCC 671).
points.apply: Pray daily: Thy kingdom come.

sub: Christians must bring the Gospel into public life (CCC 2105).
Justice, peace, dignity of life, care for the poor.
Freedom of conscience respected; the Gospel proposed, not imposed.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of justice or charity this week.

concl: Christ's Kingship is the foundation of our hope and our mission.
Every Christian shares His royal office by serving.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray Thy kingdom come with attention and do one act of justice.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, this feast is younger than many of us think. Pope Pius XI established it in 1925, in the encyclical Quas Primas. Europe had just come out of a terrible war, ideologies were rising that put the State or the race in the place of God, and many nations were living as if God did not exist. The Pope proclaimed: Christ is King, of individuals, of families and of societies.

Why is Christ King? First, by His very nature: He is the eternal Son of God, through whom and for whom all things were created (Colossians 1:15–17). Second, by conquest: He redeemed us, not with silver or gold, but with His precious blood (1 Peter 1:18–19). Third, because the Father has given Him all authority in heaven and on earth (Matthew 28:18). Daniel saw one like a son of man receiving an everlasting dominion (Daniel 7:13–14).

His Kingdom is already present and not yet complete. The Second Vatican Council says that the Church is the Kingdom of Christ already present in mystery (Lumen Gentium 3). It grows quietly like a mustard seed. But it will be fulfilled only when Christ comes again in glory, when He hands over the Kingdom to the Father and God will be all in all (1 Corinthians 15:24–28; CCC 671). Until then we pray every day: Thy kingdom come.

Does this feast have anything to say to society? Yes. The Catechism teaches that Christians have the duty to bring the spirit of the Gospel into the life of society, its customs, laws and structures (CCC 2105). That means defending the dignity of every human life from conception to natural death, working for justice and peace, caring for the poor and the migrant. It does not mean forcing faith on anyone; the Church respects freedom of conscience. We propose Christ by our witness.

Through Baptism we share in Christ's royal office, which means to serve (CCC 786). The King washed feet. So let us end this liturgical year by renewing our allegiance to Christ, and let us show it by serving the least of His brothers and sisters. Then His Kingdom will come, a little more, in our homes and in our land.

Dear brothers and sisters, a new liturgical year begins today. Our Church does not begin with a warning but with good news: an announcement. For four weeks we will listen to the angel's messages to Zechariah, to Mary and to Joseph, and prepare for the birth of the Lord.

The first two announcements are made to old people. Abraham is almost a hundred and Sarah ninety; when God promises a son, Abraham falls on his face and laughs. Centuries later Zechariah and Elizabeth are righteous, faithful, and childless, and they are old. Humanly, the story was over. But God is the God of the impossible.

Zechariah is offering incense in the Temple when the angel says: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, your prayer has been heard.” Perhaps he had stopped praying for a child long ago. God had not stopped listening. Is there a prayer you have stopped praying? This season is the time to take it up again.

And notice where salvation begins: in a family. John will turn the hearts of parents to their children. That is why St Paul speaks today of husbands and wives, parents and children: “Be subject to one another out of reverence for Christ.” Christ comes into the world through families.

So let us begin this year with hope. Let us keep the 25 Days' Fast as families, pray together, forgive one another, and make our homes ready for Jesus. God says to each of us what he said through Isaiah: “Do not fear; I have called you by name, you are mine.” Amen.
kids: Children, a new Church year starts today! It's like New Year's Day for the Church!
An angel told old Zechariah that he would have a baby boy called John. Zechariah couldn't believe it, so he couldn't speak until John was born!
God always keeps his promises. This season, let's get our hearts ready for baby Jesus. Say together: “Jesus, I'm getting ready for you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we come to the altar carrying names: parents, grandparents, a spouse, a child, a friend. We remember them with tears, but not without hope.

Ezekiel stood in a valley full of dry bones. God asked him, “Can these bones live?” Humanly the answer is no. But God spoke his word and sent his Spirit, and the bones stood up alive. For God, death is not the last word.

In the second reading Judas Maccabeus prays and offers sacrifice for soldiers who had died in sin. Scripture calls it a holy and pious thought. The Church has always prayed for the dead. Those who die in God's friendship but are not yet fully purified are helped by our prayers and above all by the Holy Qurbana.

At Bethany Martha says to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” How many of us have said the same. Jesus does not give a lecture; he gives himself: “I am the resurrection and the life.” Then he asks her, and he asks us: “Do you believe this?”
Today let us answer with Martha: “Yes, Lord, I believe.” And let our love for our dead become prayer. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. Amen.
kids: Children, do you remember someone in your family who has died?
Jesus told Martha: I am the resurrection and the life. He loves our grandparents and everyone who has died, and he will raise them up.
Some of them may still need our prayers to be fully ready for heaven. We can help them by praying.
Every night this month, let us say together: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today our Church remembers a day that changed our land: the arrival of the apostle Thomas in India. Our ancestors handed down the memory that he landed at Kodungallur, preached on this coast, founded Christian communities, and gave his life at Mylapore. We are his children in faith.

The readings tell us what an apostle is. God calls Moses and sends him with a promise. God says to his servant, chosen from the ends of the earth, “Do not fear, I am with you.” St Paul tells the Gentiles: you are no longer strangers; you are members of God's household, built on the foundation of the apostles. That is our story. We were at the ends of the earth, and through Thomas we became God's household.

In the Gospel Thomas asks an honest question: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” Jesus answers: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” Thomas did not bring our ancestors a new philosophy; he brought them a Person, the Way himself. No wonder our fathers called the faith “Margam”, the Way.

Later, touching the wounds of the risen Lord, Thomas confessed, “My Lord and my God!” That confession crossed the sea and became ours. Every time the Body of Christ is raised at the Qurbana, we say it again.

Today we also remember the Presentation of Mary, who belonged wholly to God from childhood. Let us ask Mary and Thomas to help us belong wholly to Jesus and to carry the Way to others. My Lord and my God! Amen.
kids: Children, a long, long time ago, a man got off a boat on the coast of Kerala. His name was Thomas, and he was one of Jesus' twelve friends!
He came all the way to India to tell our great-great-great-grandparents about Jesus. That's why we are Christians today!
When we see the Holy Qurbana raised up, let's say what Thomas said: “My Lord and my God!” Say it together now!

opts.a: My Lord and my God: the faith Thomas brought
intro: The faith Thomas brought to our land is summed up in his own confession: my Lord and my God (John 20:28).

sub: Unless I see (John 20:25).
Jesus shows His wounds.
My Lord and my God: the highest confession in the Gospels.
points.apply: Make the confession of Thomas at the elevation in the Holy Qurbana.

points.h: Let us go and die with Him
sub: Thomas's courage (John 11:16).
Lord, how can we know the way? (John 14:5).
Jesus: I am the Way.
points.apply: Ask Jesus to show you the way in a present decision.

points.h: Sent to the ends of the earth
sub: Tradition: arrival on the Kerala coast.
A faith received, kept and passed on.
Our mission today: Thomas Christians in many lands.
points.apply: Share the faith with the next generation, especially abroad.

concl: The faith of Thomas is our inheritance: received, kept and to be handed on.
Every Holy Qurbana echoes his confession: my Lord and my God.
opts.resolve: I will say my Lord and my God at the elevation and teach the faith to a child.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we remember with gratitude the coming of the apostle Thomas to our land. According to the ancient tradition of our Church, he landed on the coast of Kerala, preached Christ, founded communities and finally gave his life as a martyr. Let us look at Thomas in the Gospel to understand the faith he brought us.

Thomas is famous for his doubt. When the other disciples said they had seen the risen Lord, he said: unless I see the mark of the nails in His hands, and put my finger in the mark of the nails and my hand in His side, I will not believe (John 20:25). A week later Jesus came and showed him His wounds. And Thomas made the greatest confession of faith in all the Gospels: my Lord and my God (John 20:28). Doubt became adoration.

But Thomas was also courageous. When Jesus decided to go back to Judea, where His enemies wanted to stone Him, it was Thomas who said: let us also go, that we may die with Him (John 11:16). And at the Last Supper it was Thomas who asked: Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way? Jesus answered: I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:5–6).

Our ancestors called the Christian life Mar Thoma Margam, the Way of Thomas. It is the way of a faith that is honest enough to ask questions, brave enough to follow Christ to death, and humble enough to kneel and say my Lord and my God. At the elevation in every Holy Qurbana, many of us whisper those very words.

Today Thomas Christians live all over the world. The faith he brought to one coast has been carried to the Gulf, to Europe, to America, to Australia. In every place, let us keep it, live it and hand it on to our children. Like Thomas, may we see the wounds of Christ in the poor and suffering, and confess Him as our Lord and our God.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the apostolic heritage of the Syro-Malabar Church
intro: Today is a good day to learn the history and identity of our own Church.

sub: Founded on the preaching of Thomas, according to our tradition.
Communion with the East Syriac Church for centuries.
Unbroken Christian presence in India for many centuries.
points.apply: Thank God for the faith of your ancestors.

sub: Centuries of contacts and tensions.
Latinisation and the struggle for identity.
Restoration: Syro-Malabar raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church (1992).
points.apply: Pray for unity and peace in our Church.

sub: A Church sui iuris: our own liturgy, law and spirituality.
Missions in India and dioceses abroad.
Unity with the universal Church under the Pope.
points.apply: Support a mission of our Church this year.

concl: The Syro-Malabar Church is apostolic, Eastern and Catholic.
Knowing our history helps us love our Church and carry the faith forward.
opts.resolve: This month I will learn our Church's history and pray for its unity and mission.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the day we remember the coming of St Thomas, let us learn something about the identity of our Church, because many young people do not know it.

According to our ancient and living tradition, the apostle Thomas preached the Gospel in India in the first century and died as a martyr. Historians discuss the details, but the faith of the community, the songs, the place names and the very name St Thomas Christians bear witness to a Christian presence in this land from very early times. For centuries our Church lived in communion with the Church of the East and used the East Syriac liturgy, the liturgy of the Holy Qurbana of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, one of the oldest Eucharistic prayers in the world.

Our history also had trials. From the sixteenth century there were contacts and tensions with Western missionaries, Latinisation of our customs and liturgy, divisions and painful separations. Yet the community remained faithful to Christ and to the Catholic communion. Gradually the Church recovered her identity: her own bishops, her own liturgical reforms, and in 1992 the Syro-Malabar Church was raised to the status of a Major Archiepiscopal Church, governed by its Synod of Bishops under the Major Archbishop, in full communion with the Pope.

We are one of the twenty-three Eastern Catholic Churches sui iuris. That means we have our own liturgy, our own canon law, our own spirituality and theology, and we are fully Catholic. The Second Vatican Council asked Eastern Catholics to preserve their traditions faithfully (Orientalium Ecclesiarum 6). This is not a matter of pride, but of fidelity.

Today our Church has missions in many parts of India and dioceses in the Gulf, Europe, North America and Australia. Let us thank God for the faith of our ancestors, pray for unity and peace in our Church, support her missions, and above all live the faith of Thomas so that our children and grandchildren may also say with him: my Lord and my God.

Dear friends, Paul's great hymn proclaims Christ: the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation, the head of the body, the Church. All things were created through him and for him, and in him all things hold together (Colossians 1:15–18).

At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. Jesus answers that flesh and blood did not reveal this, but his Father in heaven; on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it (Matthew 16:16–18).

The Church is not only a human organisation; it is a body with Christ as its head, built on the rock of faith. This week let us make Peter's confession our own: pray the Creed slowly and from the heart, and pray for our Holy Father and our Major Archbishop. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus asked who he was, Peter said: you are the Son of the living God. Tell Jesus the same thing today!

homily: Dear friends, on the first weekday of the season of Annunciation the Church looks to the faith of Abraham. Paul reminds the Galatians that those who believe are blessed with Abraham who believed; Christ became a curse for us, so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, and we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith (Galatians 3:9, 13–14).

In the Gospel a father brings to Jesus his only son, whom the disciples could not heal. Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit, heals the boy and gives him back to his father; and all were astounded at the greatness of God (Luke 9:42–43).

Today is also the feast of St Andrew the Apostle, who, like our father St Thomas, carried Christ to distant lands. In these weeks before Christmas let us believe like Abraham and bring our children to Jesus like that father. The Twenty-Five Days Lent begins tomorrow; make your resolution today. Amen.
kids: Children, the season of Annunciation has begun! Do one good thing every day these weeks to prepare your heart for baby Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, in the season of the Dedication of the Church we reflect on our true home. Paul says that our body is a tent that will be taken down, but we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens (2 Corinthians 5:1).

The younger son learned this the hard way. He left his father's house, wasted everything, and while feeding pigs he came to himself: I will get up and go to my father. While he was still far off, his father saw him, was filled with compassion, ran and put his arms around him and kissed him (Luke 15:17–20).

The Father whom Jesus shows us is a Father who waits and runs. However far we have wandered, the door of his house is open. This week let us return to the Father's embrace through a good confession, and share with joy in the feast of the Holy Qurbana. Amen.
kids: Children, even when we do wrong, God our Father waits for us and runs to hug us. Say sorry to someone today!

homily: Dear friends, the Church is a flock with a Shepherd. Peter, who once denied the Lord, is asked three times: do you love me? And three times he receives the charge: feed my lambs, tend my sheep (John 21:15–17). Authority in the Church is born of love and exists for service.

Years later Peter himself tells the elders of the Church: tend the flock of God, not under compulsion but willingly, not lording it over those in your charge but being examples to the flock (1 Peter 5:2–3). And when the chief Shepherd appears, they will receive the crown of glory that never fades.

Let us pray today especially for our priests and bishops. And each of us is a shepherd in some way: parents, teachers, catechists. Jesus asks us too: do you love me? Let us answer with our service. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked Peter: do you love me? Today you too can say: Jesus, I love you!

homily: Dear friends, a Roman centurion, a Gentile and an officer of the occupying army, comes to Jesus for his servant. His humility and faith, Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; only speak the word, astonish Jesus: in no one in Israel have I found such faith (Matthew 8:8–10). Many will come from east and west and eat with Abraham in the kingdom of heaven.

Paul says the mystery revealed to him is that the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body and sharers in the promise in Christ Jesus (Ephesians 3:6). The door of God's house is open to every nation.

Today we remember Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth. They were righteous before God; they waited many years and kept praying, and God gave them John the Baptist. Let us pray with the humility of the centurion and the perseverance of this holy couple. Before every Holy Qurbana, let us repeat the centurion's words in our hearts. Amen.
kids: Children, Zechariah and Elizabeth prayed for many years, and God gave them John. Don't stop praying even when the answer is slow!

homily: Dear friends, a father asks his two sons to work in the vineyard. One says, I will not, but later changes his mind and goes. The other says, I go, sir, but does not go. Which of the two did the will of his father, asks Jesus (Matthew 21:28–31). Words are not enough; conversion shows itself in deeds.

Paul applies this to everyday relationships: children obey your parents; fathers, do not provoke your children but bring them up in the discipline of the Lord; servants and masters, do the will of God from the heart (Ephesians 6:1–9). Faith is tested at home and at work.

Today is the First Friday. We honour the Sacred Heart of Jesus, who obeyed the Father even unto death. Turning back is always possible. Today, let us say yes to something we said no to yesterday: an apology, a postponed duty, a neglected prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, the son who first said no later changed his mind and went. It is never too late to do the right thing. Today, do what your parents ask with a smile!

homily: Dear friends, a lawyer asks: what must I do to inherit eternal life? And then: who is my neighbour? Jesus answers with a story in which a despised Samaritan is the one who stops, binds the wounds and pays the cost (Luke 10:30–35). The question changes: not who is my neighbour, but to whom can I be a neighbour?
Paul says: let love be genuine; love one another with mutual affection; rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep (Romans 12:9–15). This is the way of life in God's house.

The Fathers of the Church compared the Church to the inn where the Samaritan brought the wounded man: a house of healing. This week let us practise love that stops: when we meet a need on the road, let us not pass by. Amen.
kids: Children, the good Samaritan stopped and helped the hurt man. If you see someone sad today, go close and help!

homily: Dear friends, near the end of his life Peter remembers the mountain: we had been eyewitnesses of his majesty; we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven while we were with him on the holy mountain (2 Peter 1:16–18). The faith of the Church rests on eyewitnesses and on the prophetic word.

That word is like a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts (2 Peter 1:19). On the mountain of the Transfiguration Jesus' face shone, and a voice came from the cloud: this is my Son, my Chosen; listen to him (Luke 9:35).

In the dark places of life we have God's word as our lamp. The Father's command, listen to him, is for us too. This week let us read the Gospel for ten minutes each day and quietly contemplate the face of Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, on the mountain Jesus' face shone like the sun. God said: listen to him. Read one word of Jesus in the Bible today!

homily: Dear friends, heaven bursts into song: Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns; the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready (Revelation 19:6–7). The whole history of salvation is a love story that ends in a wedding: Christ and his Church.

In Jesus' parable a king prepares a wedding feast for his son. The invited guests refuse to come, so the servants gather all they find on the roads, both good and bad. But the man who came without a wedding garment is put out (Matthew 22:9–13). The invitation is for all, but those who accept must prepare their hearts.

Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). Every Holy Qurbana is a foretaste of that feast. Our wedding garment is grace: received in Baptism and washed again in Confession. This Sunday let us come to the feast with a clean heart. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus invites us to a great wedding feast. The Holy Qurbana is a little taste of that feast. Come to church with joy!

homily: Dear friends, Paul says he feels a divine jealousy for the Corinthians: I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ (2 Corinthians 11:2). The apostle is like the friend who brings the bride to the bridegroom.

John the Baptist describes himself in the same way: he who has the bride is the bridegroom; the friend of the bridegroom rejoices greatly at his voice. He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:29–30).

This is the motto of every Christian and every minister: he must increase, I must decrease. In the parish and in the family, let attention turn not to me but to Jesus. Today do one good deed that no one knows about, and give the glory to Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said: Jesus must become greater, I must become less. Today do one good thing that nobody sees, just for Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, Paul speaks reluctantly of being caught up to the third heaven, into Paradise, and hearing things that cannot be told (2 Corinthians 12:2–4). Yet he refuses to boast except of his weaknesses. The heavenly vision does not make him proud; it makes him humble.
John's Gospel tells us whose testimony to believe: the one who comes from above is above all; he testifies to what he has seen and heard. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life (John 3:31–36).

We do not need to chase spiritual experiences; it is enough to believe in the Son who came from the Father's side. Let every grace we receive make us humbler. Tonight let us thank God for one grace and offer Jesus one weakness. Amen.
kids: Children, when God gives us good gifts, we should not boast but say thank you. Thank Jesus today for one gift!

homily: Dear friends, the Bible ends where it began, in a garden: the river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb; the tree of life bears fruit every month, and its leaves are for the healing of the nations. They will see his face, and there will be no more night (Revelation 22:1–5).

Jesus shows the way to that glory in the Gospel. When people brought little children to him, the disciples spoke sternly to them. But Jesus said: let the little children come to me, and do not stop them; for it is to such as these that the kingdom of heaven belongs (Matthew 19:14).

Heaven belongs to the humble and the trusting. Let nothing stop us from bringing our children to Jesus: Holy Qurbana, family prayer, catechism. And let us too take the Father's hand with the simple faith of a child. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: let the little children come to me. Jesus loves you very much! Talk to him today like a friend.

homily: Dear friends, a scribe asks which commandment is the first of all. Jesus joins two texts of the Law: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength; and love your neighbour as yourself (Mark 12:29–31). The scribe agrees that this is much more than all burnt offerings, and Jesus says: you are not far from the kingdom of God.

Paul describes what this love looks like: love is patient, love is kind; it is not envious or boastful or arrogant; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never ends (1 Corinthians 13:4–8).
Today, read these verses putting your own name in place of the word love: am I patient? am I kind? Wherever something is lacking, let us take one step forward this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: love God with all your heart and love others as yourself. Be patient with a friend today!

homily: Dear friends, Paul calls the apostles servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries, and says that it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy (1 Corinthians 4:1–2). Everything we have, money, time and faith, is entrusted to us; we are managers, not owners.

In the parable of the dishonest manager Jesus says: whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. You cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:10–13). Money is a good servant but a bad master.

Today the Church also remembers St Elizabeth of Hungary, a princess who saw her wealth as belonging to the poor. Let us set aside a share of our income for God and the poor, and honour the Lord with what we have. Amen.
kids: Children, everything we have is a gift from God. Today set aside a little of your pocket money for the poor!

homily: Dear friends, after listing the sins that exclude from the Kingdom, Paul adds with tenderness: and this is what some of you used to be. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God (1 Corinthians 6:11).

Baptism is a real change: a new identity in Christ. Christians are called to live as people who have been washed, not taking their quarrels before unbelievers, but dealing justly with their brothers and sisters. Jesus also says that everyone tries to enter the Kingdom by force (Luke 16:16), with eager resolve.
Our past does not decide our future; God's grace does. Today let us renew our baptismal promises in our hearts, and take the first step to settle a family quarrel with love. Amen.
kids: Children, at Baptism God washed us and made us new. When you enter the church today, make the sign of the cross and remember: I am God's child.

homily: Dear friends, Paul thanks God that the Gospel is bearing fruit and growing in the whole world, and prays that the Colossians may lead lives worthy of the Lord, bearing fruit in every good work (Colossians 1:6, 10). The Church is God's field.

Jesus explains the parable of the sower: the same seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil. The one who hears the word and understands it bears fruit, a hundredfold, sixtyfold, thirtyfold (Matthew 13:18–23). The difference is not in the seed but in the soil.

What kind of soil is my heart today? A path trodden hard by hurry, shallow rock, or thorns of worry? Let us pull out one thorn this week: one hour less on the phone, one hour more with the Word. Amen.
kids: Children, God's word is like a seed. Listen carefully so you can be good soil! Tell your family one word you heard in church today.

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews reminds suffering Christians that the Lord disciplines those whom he loves. Discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness (Hebrews 12:6, 11). Hardship received in faith is the Father's training.
Jesus says: I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinegrower. Every branch that bears fruit he prunes to make it bear more fruit. Abide in me; apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:1–5).
Pruning hurts, but it is a sign of the gardener's love. Offer Jesus one difficulty you are going through now, and stay united to the vine through daily prayer and the Holy Qurbana. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the vine and we are the branches. If we stay close to Jesus we bear good fruit: kindness, patience and joy!

homily: Dear friends, in the last week of the year the Church hears again the promise of the Father's house: do not let your hearts be troubled. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places; I go to prepare a place for you (John 14:1–2). Thomas the Apostle asks: how can we know the way? Jesus answers: I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:5–6).

Paul says that in Christ the dividing wall has been broken down: you are no longer strangers and aliens, but citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, built on Christ the cornerstone, growing into a dwelling place for God in the Spirit (Ephesians 2:19–22).

The Church on earth is the porch of that house. As the season of the Dedication of the Church ends, let us ask: am I a visitor in my parish, or a member of God's household? This week let us decide to take an active part in one ministry of the parish. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: I am the way. If we follow Jesus, we will reach the Father's house in heaven!

homily: Dear friends, Peter gives to the baptised the titles God gave Israel at Sinai: you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light (1 Peter 2:9). Once you were not a people; now you are God's people.

Jesus is the gate for the sheep: I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly. I have other sheep that do not belong to this fold; I must bring them also, so there will be one flock, one shepherd (John 10:10, 16).

Royal priesthood means that our whole life is an offering to God: work, family, sufferings. Today, at the Holy Qurbana or in prayer at home, offer your whole day as a gift, and invite back into the flock one sheep who has drifted away. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the good shepherd who wants to gather all his sheep together. Today invite a friend who is alone to join your game!

homily: Dear friends, Paul's great blessing opens the mystery of the whole year: blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places, just as he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:3–4).

Mary sings the same joy in her Magnificat: my soul magnifies the Lord, for he has looked with favour on the lowliness of his servant. He has brought down the powerful from their thrones and lifted up the lowly (Luke 1:46–52). Mary's song is the Church's song.

As the season of the Dedication of the Church comes to an end, let us thank God with Mary for the blessings of a whole year. This evening, sit together as a family, name five blessings of this year, and pray a rosary of thanksgiving. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary sang a song of praise to God. Today thank God for five good things he gave you this year!

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews says: here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come (Hebrews 13:14). The Church is a pilgrim people; our true citizenship is in heaven. Meanwhile we offer God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess his name, and we do not neglect to do good and to share what we have (Hebrews 13:15–16).

The seventy-two return from their mission full of joy: Lord, in your name even the demons submit to us. Jesus says: rejoice that your names are written in heaven. At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit: I thank you, Father, because you have revealed these things to infants (Luke 10:17–21).
Pilgrims travel light and keep a joyful heart. Our joy is not in our successes, but in the fact that God knows us. Today let us sing a hymn of praise, and share what we have with someone. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says your names are written in heaven. How wonderful! Sing a song to Jesus today.

homily: Dear friends, the Sadducees, who denied the resurrection, try to ridicule it with the story of a woman married to seven brothers. Jesus answers that they are wrong because they know neither the scriptures nor the power of God. In the resurrection life is transformed; and God is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; he is God not of the dead but of the living (Mark 12:24–27).

The Book of Revelation shows us those living ones: a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, robed in white, with palm branches in their hands, crying out: salvation belongs to our God and to the Lamb (Revelation 7:9–10).
In that multitude are our beloved dead, and generations of St Thomas Christians. Let us remember them today before the God of the living, and prepare our lives to join them in eternal praise. Amen.
kids: Children, in heaven people from every country praise God together. Pray today for your grandparents or others who have died.

homily: Dear friends, on the last day of the season of the Dedication of the Church we see Jacob dreaming of a ladder set up on the earth, its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God ascending and descending on it. Jacob wakes and says: this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven (Genesis 28:12–17). Every church, every Holy Qurbana, is a gate of heaven.

Today we keep in advance the feast of St Andrew. By the Sea of Galilee Jesus calls Peter and Andrew: follow me, and I will make you fish for people. Immediately they left their nets and followed him (Matthew 4:19–20). Paul says that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved; but how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him (Romans 10:13–14)?

The first thing Andrew did was to bring his brother to Jesus. Tomorrow the season of Annunciation begins. Decide today to bring one person to Jesus this Christmas season: your brother or sister, or a friend. Amen.
kids: Children, when Andrew met Jesus he ran and brought his brother. Invite a friend to church too!

intro: Theme: “The Bride keeps her lamp burning.”

Qudash Edtha begins: the Church contemplates herself as God's dwelling and as the Bride awaiting the Bridegroom. The tent of meeting, the true sanctuary entered by Christ, and the wise virgins frame today's message.

points.h: The tent of meeting: friendship with God
sub: Moses pitches the tent outside the camp; all who seek the Lord go out to it.
God speaks with Moses “face to face, as one speaks to a friend.”
The Church is our tent of meeting; prayer is friendship, not formality.
q: Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.

But when Christ came as a high priest of the good things that have come, then through the greater and perfect tent (not made with hands, that is, not of this creation), he entered once for all into the Holy Place.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

sub: The psalmist faints with longing for the courts of the Lord.
Christ has opened the sanctuary with his own blood; the Qurbana is our entry.
Love for the parish church is love for the place where heaven touches earth.
q: How lovely is your dwelling place, O LORD of hosts! My soul longs, indeed it faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
Not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.
points.apply: Arrive early for the Qurbana next Sunday and prepare in silence.

sub: Five virgins took oil with their lamps; five did not.
Faith, prayer and love cannot be borrowed when the Bridegroom arrives.
Those who wait for the Lord renew their strength.
q: But those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
And while they went to buy it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went with him into the wedding banquet; and the door was shut.
points.apply: Choose one daily habit of prayer for the four weeks of Qudash Edtha.

concl: The Church ends her year with the Bridegroom's question: are you ready?
Let us store oil day by day and enter with him into the feast.
2026-11-01.resolve: Keep a small lamp or candle lit at family prayer each evening this week.

intro: Theme: “The inheritance that does not fade.”
From the promised land to the heavenly inheritance: God gives himself to his people, and what we leave for Christ returns a hundredfold.

sub: In Egypt God promises freedom, a people and a land.
The greatest gift is God himself: “I will be your God.”
The Church is the people on the way to the inheritance.
q: I will take you as my people, and I will be your God. You shall know that I am the LORD your God, who has freed you from the burdens of the Egyptians.
And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or fields, for my name's sake, will receive a hundredfold, and will inherit eternal life.
points.apply: Thank God for the freedom he has given you in Christ.

sub: The Servant's reward is with God, even when his labour seems vain.
Peter: an inheritance imperishable, undefiled, unfading.
Faith, not property, is the family's true wealth.
q: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot. The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; I have a goodly heritage.

By his great mercy he has given us a new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you.
points.apply: Tell your children how faith came to your family.

points.h: Impossible for us, possible for God
sub: Riches cannot open the door of the Kingdom.
Salvation is God's work; we receive it with open hands.
The apostles who left everything will share Christ's glory.
q: But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my cause is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.”
But Jesus looked at them and said, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.”
points.apply: Give something valuable to someone in need this week.

concl: What we keep we lose; what we give to Christ we keep forever.
Let us leave our children the inheritance of faith.
2026-11-08.resolve: Read 1 Peter 1:3–9 as a family this week.

intro: Theme: “Well done, good and trustworthy servant.”
At the end of the liturgical year the Lord asks what we have done with his gifts: love that makes labour light, faithful work while we wait, talents invested and not buried.

sub: Jacob's seven years seemed a few days because of love.
Love transforms duty into gift.
Work done for God and others is never wasted.
q: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
points.apply: Offer tomorrow's work to God for someone you love.

points.h: Faithful in duty while we wait
sub: Sirach: grow old in your work and trust the Lord.
Paul: waiting for Christ is no excuse for idleness.
Honest work is part of holiness.
q: Stand by your agreement and attend to it, and grow old in your work.
Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
points.apply: Do a full day's honest work without cutting corners.

sub: Each received “according to his ability”.
Fear buries the talent; faith invests it.
The faithful enter the joy of the master.
q: Go to the ant, you lazybones; consider its ways, and be wise.
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and trustworthy slave; you have been trustworthy in a few things, I will put you in charge of many things; enter into the joy of your master.’
points.apply: Offer one skill to your parish this month.

concl: God does not ask what we do not have, but what we have.
May we hear: “Enter into the joy of your master.”
2026-11-15.resolve: List three gifts God has given you and how you will use them before Christmas.

intro: Theme: “Jesus, reign in me.”

On the last Sunday of the year the Church proclaims Christ the King: Priest-King prefigured by Melchizedek, rejected by Israel's demand for an earthly king, crowned with thorns before Pilate, and revealed as King of kings.

sub: Melchizedek, king of Salem, offers bread and wine and blesses Abraham.
Christ is the eternal Priest-King.
At the Qurbana the King gives himself to us.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High. He blessed him and said, “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, maker of heaven and earth.”
He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is called The Word of God.
points.apply: Receive Communion this Sunday as an act of homage to your King.

sub: Israel demands a king “like other nations”.
God says: they have rejected me.
We do the same when money, power or opinion rule us.
q: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from being king over them.”

Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my followers would be fighting to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”
points.apply: Name one thing that rules you instead of God, and dethrone it.

sub: Daniel sees the Son of Man receive an everlasting kingdom.
Christ reigns by truth: whoever belongs to the truth hears his voice.
At the end every knee will bow.
q: To him was given dominion and glory and kingship, that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that shall not pass away.
On his robe and on his thigh he has a name inscribed, “King of kings and Lord of lords.”
points.apply: Consecrate your family to Christ the King this week.

concl: The year ends at the feet of the King.
Let him reign in our homes, our work and our hearts.
2026-11-22.resolve: Pray the Litany or an act of consecration to Christ the King as a family.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid; your prayer has been heard.”
The new year begins with the announcement of John's birth, echoing the promise of Isaac, and with the family as the place where Christ's coming is prepared.

sub: Abraham and Sarah are too old; Abraham laughs.
God keeps his promise and gives Isaac.
What is impossible for us is possible for God.
q: God said, “No, but your wife Sarah shall bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.”
But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.”
points.apply: Take up again one prayer you had given up.

sub: God redeems and calls his people by name.
No one is forgotten in God's plan.
The new year is a new call.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Both of them were righteous before God, living blamelessly according to all the commandments and regulations of the Lord.
points.apply: Thank God for calling you by name in baptism.

sub: John comes in the spirit of Elijah.
He turns the hearts of parents to children.
The family prepares the way of the Lord.
q: He will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.

With the spirit and power of Elijah he will go before him, to turn the hearts of parents to their children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
points.apply: Plan the 25 Days' Fast together as a family.

concl: God keeps his promises; the year begins in hope.
Let our families be ready for the Lord.
2026-11-29.resolve: Pray together as a family every evening of the 25 Days' Fast.

intro: Theme: “Love that death does not end.”
On the Commemoration of the Dead we pray for the faithful departed, confessing the resurrection of the body and the communion of saints.

sub: Ezekiel's valley of dry bones: what seems final is not final for God.
God's word and Spirit bring life where there is none.
q: And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people. I will put my spirit within you, and you shall live.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live.”
points.apply: Bring one hopeless situation to God in prayer this week.

sub: Judas Maccabeus offers sacrifice for the dead.
The Church prays for souls being purified (CCC 1030–1032); the Qurbana is the greatest help.
q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
points.apply: Have a Qurbana offered for the souls in purgatory this month.

sub: The souls of the righteous are in God's hand.
Even in the darkest valley the Shepherd is with us.
q: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them.
And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?
points.apply: Visit the cemetery with your family and pray there.

concl: Our grief is real; our hope is greater, because it is Christ himself.
Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.
2026-11-02.resolve: Pray for your departed by name every evening in November.

intro: Theme: “The Father's house.”
Paul longs for the eternal dwelling; the prodigal son returns home and is embraced.

sub: God's love for us is everlasting and faithful.
Even when we wander, he does not stop loving.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Thank God today for one sign of his faithful love.

sub: Hunger made the son remember his father's house.
Conversion is coming back to the truth about ourselves and God.
q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?
For this son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found!” And they began to celebrate.
points.apply: Examine your conscience tonight.

sub: Our body is a tent; heaven is our house.
The Church is the doorway to the Father's house.
q: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Plan a good confession this month.

concl: The Father is watching the road.
Let us go home.
2026-11-03.resolve: Make a good confession before the end of the liturgical year.

intro: Theme: “Love first, then feed.”
Peter's threefold confession of love becomes a threefold mission.

sub: God himself promised to search for his flock.
Jesus fulfils it as the Good Shepherd.
q: For thus says the Lord GOD: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.

When they had finished breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my lambs.”
points.apply: Pray for someone who has drifted from the Church.

sub: God promised shepherds who would feed with knowledge.
Pastors serve, not dominate.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.
points.apply: Pray for your bishop and parish priest by name.

sub: Every Christian shepherds someone.
We lead best by example.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you.”
points.apply: Speak to a younger person about your faith this week.

concl: Love for Christ is the root of all service.
Let us love him, and feed his sheep.
2026-11-04.resolve: Offer a decade of the Rosary for priests each day this week.

intro: Theme: “Only say the word.”
A Gentile centurion's faith opens the vision of all nations at the banquet of the Kingdom.

sub: The centurion believes that Jesus' word is enough.
Humility is the doorway of faith.
q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but only speak the word, and my servant will be healed.”
points.apply: Say the centurion's words slowly before Communion.

sub: The prophets foresaw all nations streaming to God's house.
We Indians are among those who came from the east.
q: In days to come the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established as the highest of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; all the nations shall stream to it.
I tell you, many will come from east and west and will eat with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Pray for missionaries from Kerala serving abroad.

points.h: A house of prayer for all
sub: God's house is open to all peoples.
Zechariah and Elizabeth kept praying through long waiting.
q: For my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
When Jesus heard him, he was amazed and said to those who followed him, “Truly I tell you, in no one in Israel have I found such faith.”
points.apply: Pray for one sick person you know.

concl: One word of Jesus is enough.
Let us come to him with humble faith.
2026-11-05.resolve: Pray for the sick of your parish this week.

intro: Theme: “Yes in deeds.”
The parable of the two sons and Paul's teaching on work call us to obedience that acts. First Friday: the Sacred Heart.

sub: God desires the sinner's conversion, not his death.
The son who refused later repented and went.
q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?

For John came to you in the way of righteousness and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.
points.apply: Turn back today from one sin you have excused.

points.h: Doing God's will from the heart
sub: Work, family duties and relationships become service of Christ.
God sees what is done from the heart.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Offer your day's work to the Sacred Heart.

points.h: The Heart that obeyed to the end
sub: Jesus' Heart did the Father's will in love.
The pierced Heart is the source of the sacraments.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Make an act of consecration to the Sacred Heart today.

concl: God looks for deeds, not only words.
Let our yes be real, like the Heart of Jesus.
2026-11-06.resolve: Keep one postponed promise to God today.

intro: Theme: “Go and do likewise.”
The Good Samaritan and Paul's portrait of genuine love.

sub: The commandment is already in the Law of Moses.
Jesus joins love of God and love of neighbour.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
